title: The fee has no home in rwb-litigation and no named payment operation on rwb-payment
source: 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epics 3 to 8 v3.md (RWB-E5-015, story, data table, endpoints and messages); 03 Requirements and specifications/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v7/Recovery Workbench FSD S4 Litigation and enforcement v4.md A2.15; 05 Technical architecture/Recovery Workbench Technical Specifications by Module v6/Recovery Workbench TSD S4 Litigation and enforcement v3.md T3.1, T-A.1 and T5.2.2; _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Business Rules and Routing Logic v4.md rows R-LIT-41 to R-LIT-43; _work/msr/context/S4.md
section: RWB-S4-E5015-APP sections 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 (X8, X10), 7 (AC1), 8 (BR1), 11, 12.1, 12.2, 12.8, 13, 15, 19; RWB-S4-E5015-CON sections 1, 2, 3, 7 (AC1, AC3), 8 (BR1), 11, 12.1, 12.2, 12.8, 19; the metadata rows and the two fragments
description: The legacy story says the step checks the fee, routes it and 'pays it', and R-LIT-42 says 'raise the fee and post it against the case' with the systems 'ALS core and GL'. No part of rwb-litigation can hold or pay it: the ownership rows of the service name only hearing and legal_action as its tables, neither of which carries a fee, a spend, an amount to pay or a posting column in TSD S4 T3.1, and the service owns no fee resource among its five operations. The fee therefore belongs to P8 rwb-payment, the module 'Payments and posting', but rwb-payment appears in no dependency row of this key, in no metadata row and in no ownership row of S4, and no source read names a payment operation, a field list or a fee table. The legacy prerequisite FEAT-PAY-05 names the dependency as a feature only, and the endpoint table of the legacy key gives the step no money operation of its own.
evidence: Context pack: 'Tables (2) hearing, legal_action'; 'REST operations provided (5)'; 'Events (0)'; 'Jobs (0)'; 'Workflows (1) LitigationWorkflow'. TSD S4 T3.1 gives legal_action fourteen fields (DF-LEG-001 to DF-LEG-014) and hearing six (DF-LEG-024 to DF-LEG-029), none of them a fee, an amount to pay or a posting; T-A.1 gives five operations and none of them touches money. Business Rules and Routing Logic v4: R-LIT-41 'Route the fee to the approver inside the D7.4 limit', R-LIT-42 'Raise the fee and post it against the case', systems 'ALS core and GL', R-LIT-43 'Record the reason and return the case without the spend'. FSD S4 A2.15.2: 'Integration points. Partner portal, ALS and GL'; 'Prerequisites. FEAT-PAY-05'. The metadata rows of both stories carry Contract, Integration and External dependencies None.
area: Application and contract, S4 rwb-litigation with P8 rwb-payment
owner_role: Solution architect, S4 rwb-litigation, with the P8 rwb-payment architect and the business owner of S4
proposed: Keep the legacy sentence unchanged with its origin tag and record the target reading: the approved fee is paid and posted against the case by rwb-payment on its contract (one hop, 2 s, faked, operation name left as the placeholder); this service checks the fee, routes it, records the decision and stores the payment reference, and posts nothing; rwb-payment appears on the contract rows of both stories, and the metadata rows stay exactly as the plan gives them.

title: The fee schedule has no field list, no owner row and no version in any source
source: 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epics 3 to 8 v3.md (RWB-E5-015: 'checks the fee against the schedule'); 03 Requirements and specifications/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v7/Recovery Workbench FSD S4 Litigation and enforcement v4.md A2.15.1 to A2.15.3; 05 Technical architecture/Recovery Workbench Technical Specifications by Module v6/Recovery Workbench TSD S4 Litigation and enforcement v3.md T3.1 and T3.2; _work/msr/context/S4.md (short DP table rows DP-06 and DP-07)
description: The legacy behaviour is defined against 'the schedule' and BR-S4-015 requires that no value a business person may change is written in code, but no source read for this key gives the schedule a name, a field list, a version, a row set or an owner: FSD S4 A2.15 names only the rule IDs R-LIT-30, VR-S4-015-1 and BR-S4-015, TSD S4 T3.1 and T3.2 carry no fee list, and the ownership rows of S4 carry no reference table. DP-06 and DP-07, which would give the schedule a platform H row and a C row to rwb-case, are outside the pattern set of the key, so the read would carry no dependency row even once its owner is confirmed.
evidence: FSD S4 A2.15.1: 'Checks the fee against the schedule, routes it for approval where needed and pays it'. A2.15.3.1 lists VR-S4-015-1, R-LIT-30 and BR-S4-015 only, with no schedule identifier and no court-level list. TSD S4 T3.2 gives four lists of values, none of them a fee type or a court level; T3.1 gives legal_action claim_amount as the amount in dispute, not a fee. Context pack short DP table: DP-06 (parameters of rwb-case) and DP-07 (reference data of rwb-case) each add H RWB-PLT-E1042-CON or RWB-PLT-E1043-CON and a C row; the WP legacy record carries patterns DP03, DP13, DP19 and C empty.
area: Rules and reference data, S4 rwb-litigation with P3 rwb-case
owner_role: Solution architect, S4 rwb-litigation, with the P3 rwb-case reference-data owner and the business owner of S4
proposed: Read the fee schedule, the fee types and the court levels as versioned reference data of rwb-case on its contract, name the read on the contract rows of both stories with the operation name left as the placeholder, carry the schedule version on every decision record, and leave the metadata rows as the plan gives them.

title: Legacy AC2 of this key carries R-LIT-30, a filing rule already owned by two sibling stories, and the spend states are not values of LOV-LEGAL-STATUS
source: 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epics 3 to 8 v3.md (RWB-E5-015 AC2; RWB-E5-010 AC3); _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Business Rules and Routing Logic v4.md row R-LIT-30; 05 Technical architecture/Recovery Workbench Technical Specifications by Module v6/Recovery Workbench TSD S4 Litigation and enforcement v3.md T3.2 and T4; 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench Service Story Files v1/RWB-SVC-S4 rwb-litigation (Litigation)/RWB S4 E5010 APP Record the court filing and receipt v1.md sections 1, 7 and 9
description: Two overlaps are recorded. (1) AC2 of RWB-E5-015 is the filing rule R-LIT-30 — 'write the court case number to the Legal Action and set the hearing timers' and the move to FILED_IN_COURT — and the same rule row and the same state move are owned by RWB-E5-010 AC3 and by the hearing story of this service, which build the court case number on `legal_action.black_case_no` and the timers of `LitigationWorkflow`. A second build of either would be a second writer of the same column and a second timer for the same date. (2) The spend states LEGAL_SPEND_APPROVAL and IN_HEARING are case route states of rwb-case and are not values of LOV-LEGAL-STATUS, so no list value may be invented for them in this service.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E5-015 AC2: 'Given a case in state FIRM_INSTRUCTED / When case filed / Then write the court case number to the Legal Action and set the hearing timers / Then the case moves to FILED_IN_COURT'. Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 R-LIT-30: from FIRM_INSTRUCTED, event CASE_FILED, to FILED_IN_COURT, timer 'Filing service level by task'. `RWB-S4-E5010-APP` section 1 lists R-LIT-30 as its own rule and section 9 as its own transition; `RWB-S4-E5011-APP` section 12.5 hosts the hearing timers. TSD S4 T3.2: LOV-LEGAL-STATUS is OPEN, FILED, JUDGMENT, ENFORCING, CLOSED, WITHDRAWN.
area: Scope and state model, S4 rwb-litigation
owner_role: Solution architect, S4 rwb-litigation, with the story owners of RWB-S4-E5010 and RWB-S4-E5011
proposed: Keep AC2 word for word with its origin tag and prove it as a post-condition of the filing and hearing stories' surfaces against the contract fakes: this story writes no `black_case_no` and arms no hearing timer. Record the spend states as case route states read from the rwb-case answer and invent no LOV value for them.

title: The D7.4 limit, the approval row and the rule-package read carry no value and no dependency row
source: _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Business Rules and Routing Logic v4.md rows R-LIT-41, R-LIT-42 and R-LIT-43; 05 Technical architecture/Recovery Workbench Technical Specifications by Module v6/Recovery Workbench TSD S4 Litigation and enforcement v3.md T5.2.2 and T6.1; 03 Requirements and specifications/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v7/Recovery Workbench FSD S4 Litigation and enforcement v4.md A2.15.3; _work/msr/context/S4.md (short DP table rows DP-04 and DP-08)
description: R-LIT-41 routes the fee 'to the approver inside the D7.4 limit' and R-LIT-42 pays it 'inside the limit, or the committee approves above it', but no source read for this key gives the D7.4 limit a value, a field list, a currency or an owner role beyond 'Approver at D7.4', and the committee path above the limit has no documented threshold. The approval itself is a named consumed contract — TSD S4 T5.2.2 row 'Approval, Temporal child workflow, P7 rwb-decision, class C' — but no dependency row, H, C or I, carries it, and the rule-package read of DP-04 has no row either, because DP-04 is outside the pattern set. The delegation limit would arrive with DP-08 (authorise contract of rwb-access), which is also outside the set.
evidence: Business Rules and Routing Logic v4: R-LIT-41 approver 'Approver at D7.4', SLA '3 working days'; R-LIT-42 'inside the limit, or the committee approves above it', systems 'ALS core and GL', SLA '5 working days'; R-LIT-43 'the approver rejects the spend', SLA 'None'. TSD S4 T5.2.2 lists the Approval child workflow as consumed class C. TSD S4 T6.1 gives the Litigation rights of thirty roles and no limit. Context pack short DP table: DP-04 adds H RWB-PLT-E1072-CON and C RWB-P7-E1073-CON; DP-08 adds H RWB-PLT-E1037-CON and C RWB-P4-E1037-CON. The WP legacy record carries C, I and X empty.
area: Approval and rules, S4 rwb-litigation with P7 rwb-decision, P4 rwb-access and the platform library
owner_role: Solution architect, S4 rwb-litigation, with the P7 rwb-decision, P4 rwb-access and platform library architects and the business owner of S4
proposed: Declare the approval as the P7 child workflow consumed on queue rwb-decision, the D7.4 limit and the approver's delegation as consumed on the rwb-access authorise contract, and the LITIGATION package with R-LIT-30 and R-LIT-41 to R-LIT-43 as consumed from rwb-decision, each with the placeholder on its operation name and ceiling; fix no limit value in code or in the document, and leave the metadata rows as the plan gives them.

title: No requirement identifier exists for FEAT-LIT-15 and the S4 module extracts are absent from the run folder
source: 05 Technical architecture/Recovery Workbench Technical Specifications by Module v6/Recovery Workbench TSD S4 Litigation and enforcement v3.md T8 and T0.1; 03 Requirements and specifications/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v7/Recovery Workbench FSD S4 Litigation and enforcement v4.md FEAT-LIT-15 row; 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epics 3 to 8 v3.md (RWB-E5-015 metadata: Feature FEAT-LIT-15, Priority Must); _work/msr/extract (no file whose name contains S4)
section: RWB-S4-E5015-APP sections 2, 18, 19; RWB-S4-E5015-CON sections 2, 18; the reqs keys of both fragments and the Traceability tables
description: TSD S4 T8 maps REQ-S4-001 to REQ-S4-010 to FEAT-LIT-01 only, the FSD S4 feature table gives FEAT-LIT-15 with no requirement column, and the legacy master carries no requirement ID for the key, so this story can trace only to the feature, to the rules and to the module measure. Separately, the read list of the work package names the FSD and TSD module extracts of S4 in _work/msr/extract, and no such file exists: the module documents were read from their source folders, so a later check that re-reads the extract folder will not find them.
evidence: TSD S4 T8: ten rows, REQ-S4-001 to REQ-S4-010, all against FEAT-LIT-01, story 'Written one epic ahead'. FSD S4 line 104: '| S4 | FEAT-LIT-15 | Pay court fees and legal expenses | System | ... | E5 | A2.15 |'. Legacy RWB-E5-015 metadata: 'Feature | FEAT-LIT-15 Pay court fees and legal expenses', 'Priority | Must', 'Depends on | FEAT-PAY-05'. Directory listing of _work/msr/extract: 18 files, none containing 'S4'.
area: Traceability and run material, S4 rwb-litigation
owner_role: Business analyst of EP05 with the S4 tech lead and the run coordinator
proposed: Trace the story to FEAT-LIT-15, to R-LIT-30 and R-LIT-41 to R-LIT-43 and to the module measure 'litigation turnaround, 6 days', leave the reqs keys empty as the plan gives them, and add the S4 module extracts to the run folder at the next assembly step so the citations and the extract agree.
